e: Two SQS queues decouple order collection from fulfillment and hold orders durably so nothing is lost during scaling, and scaling each Auto Scaling group on the number of messages in its queue (backlog) matches capacity to actual demand. CPU-based scaling, minimum capacity at peak, or scaling on queue notifications don't track the backlog.

DynamoDB global tables provide automatic multi-Region, active-active replication for continuous availability and resilience, and provisioned capacity with auto scaling is the most cost-effective for a steady, growing workload. Manual or Streams-based replication adds work, and global tables don't fit a single-Region table setup.

An S3 File Gateway deployed on premises caches frequently used data locally for low-latency access while the data stays in S3, which is cost-effective. Copying the data to FSx adds cost, Mountpoint for S3 doesn't give the same low-latency local caching, and an on-premises file server defeats the purpose.

AWS Global Accelerator routes international customers' traffic onto the AWS global network at the nearest edge location and to the Regional endpoint, speeding up dynamic API calls cost-effectively with no application changes. CloudFront caching doesn't help dynamic API responses much, and Direct Connect or VPNs per customer are costly.

API Gateway with SQS buffers surges of survey submissions, Lambda polls the queue and calls Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis, and DynamoDB with a 365-day TTL stores results for 12 months, all serverless and scalable. EC2-based APIs don't scale as well, and Rekognition and Lex aren't for text sentiment.

The AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalancerInstance Automation document deregisters instances from the load balancer, patches them, and registers them again, but it works with instance-type target groups, so change the target type from IP to instance. The existing document, State Manager, or Maintenance Windows alone don't handle deregistration this way.

AWS Glue is serverless ETL for the extract-transform-load pipeline with the least operational effort, and a Glue security configuration with client-side encryption using customer-specific KMS keys (CSE-KMS) encrypts the data where it's processed before it reaches S3. SSE-S3 isn't customer-specific, and EMR clusters per customer add overhead.

An Auto Scaling group from a launch template with an ALB scales the stateless application automatically, and using Spot capacity (acceptable since the app is resilient and stateless) is the cheapest option. Manually adding a second instance or resizing instances doesn't scale seamlessly.

An S3 Bucket Key for SSE-KMS lets S3 generate short-lived bucket-level keys from the KMS key, sharply reducing the number of KMS requests (and their cost) for frequently accessed objects while keeping KMS encryption. SSE-S3 or SSE-C don't use KMS, and client-side encryption still calls KMS.

AWS Application Migration Service performs lift-and-shift: install the replication agent on the VMs, finish the initial replication and launch test instances for acceptance testing, then stop operations and launch the cutover instances. SCT, DMS, and App2Container aren't VM rehost tools.

A Cognito identity pool exchanges the user pool login for temporary AWS credentials scoped to S3 access, and an S3 VPC (gateway) endpoint lets the application in the private subnet reach S3 privately. User pools alone don't issue AWS credentials, and IP-based or NAT-based restrictions are weaker.

The processing tier is CPU-bound with an unpredictable backlog in SQS, so a target tracking policy that scales the processing Auto Scaling group on the queue's ApproximateNumberOfMessages (backlog per instance) adds capacity when needed. Scheduled scaling can't handle unpredictable peaks, and caching doesn't relieve processing CPU.

Instances that run constantly Monday to Saturday suit Standard Reserved Instances (largest discount), and instances needed only 12 hours on Sunday that can't be interrupted fit Scheduled Reserved Instances (recurring weekly schedule), while Spot can be interrupted. This is the exam's intended answer, though Scheduled RIs are no longer sold to new customers.

AWS Batch runs the image processing jobs without managing infrastructure and scales with the number of jobs, Step Functions orchestrates the workflow and removes manual steps, and S3 stores the large output files. EC2 and ECS-on-Spot designs require infrastructure management.

CloudFront in front of the S3 bucket speeds up downloads through edge caching, and S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads from distant users, both enabled by configuration with the least effort. Multi-Region EC2 or replicated buckets are more work, and Global Accelerator doesn't front S3 directly.

An S3 gateway endpoint with the route table updated keeps S3 traffic on the AWS network and has no hourly or data processing charges, making it the cheapest way to avoid the internet. Interface endpoints cost more, and NAT gateway approaches still use the internet path.

IAM Roles for Service Accounts gives each Kubernetes service account its own IAM role: the UI service account gets DynamoDB access and the data services account gets S3 access, so each pod type can reach only its service. Attaching both policies to the node instance profile would give every pod both, and policies can't be attached directly to pods. Option D reverses the services.

AD Connector links IAM Identity Center to the existing on-premises Active Directory, and permission sets assign each AD group access to specific accounts and resources across the organization, giving centralized identity management with the least overhead. Per-developer IAM users, Cognito, or a separate managed AD with trust add work.

An API Gateway resource policy can allow or deny access by source IP address, so a policy that denies any IP not in the trusted list restricts the API to the company's network. Security groups and network ACLs don't attach to API Gateway, and private integrations connect to backends rather than restrict callers.
